messages:
marta: AMS GPU cluster networking is ready for final validation and handoff. TGW attachments done, route tables propagated, and two NAT gateways provisioned. Need someone to run the quick smoke list and sanity-check DNS delegation before we mark this as production-ready.

ryan: On it. Can you paste the exact checks you want so I don't miss anything? Trying to keep this under 30m.

marta: Quick checklist (do in order):
1) Confirm TGW attachments show 'available' for all acct vpcs and ams-uc1-gpu cluster.
2) Validate route propagation: ensure route tables in cluster subnets point to TGW for 0.0.0.0/0 and that local routes for pod/eni CIDRs exist.
3) Verify NAT GW elastic IPs allocated and associated, and that SNAT works from worker nodes.
4) DNS: confirm delegated zone for ams.redwood-inference.internal is in place and that glue records exist in our parent zone.
5) BGP/border checks for transit: check prefixes and no unexpected blackholes.
6) Smoke: curl model-serving health endpoint behind ALB from a test VM in the same subnet and from an external egress path.

Paste of a couple helpful commands:
```bash
# TGW attachments
aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters "Name=resource-id,Values=vpc-ams-uc1"

# Route table check
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-ams-*" --query 'RouteTables[].Routes'

# NAT GW list
aws ec2 describe-nat-gateways --filter "Name=tag:Name,Values=ams-nat-*"

# quick curl smoke from bastion
curl -sS http://10.12.34.56:8080/health || true
```

sung: ran the TGW attachment check, all attachments show available except the hub-to-edge link shows a transient state earlier. I ran `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --transit-gateway-attachment-ids tgw-attach-0a1b2c` and saw `State: available` now. Also noticed a flapping BGP session on the transit router for prefix 10.200.0.0/16 — saw periodic "Estab" -> "Down" in the router logs about 10:12-10:15 UTC.

ryan: which router? can you paste the snippet? might be noisy from our maintenance window.

sung: snippet:
```
Mar 10 10:12:02 bgpd[1244]: neighbor 192.0.2.5 down: Connection reset by peer
Mar 10 10:12:05 bgpd[1244]: neighbor 192.0.2.5 up: BGP Open Confirm
Mar 10 10:15:01 bgpd[1244]: neighbor 192.0.2.5 down: hold time expired
```
I restarted the session from our side, neighbor came back. No prefixes were withdrawn for more than 3 minutes.

jules: cost flag: two NAT gateways (one per AZ) will add ~\u20ac0.15/hr each plus EIP charges. For light traffic we should consider centralizing egress through a regional NAT or using an autoscaling NAT instance fleet behind a small ALB to save cost while we ramp. Thoughts?

marta: good call. For now we kept the two NAT GW per AZ since it's the standard for High Availability. For Dedicated customers we might later centralize to cut unit cost. Handoff note: if we choose NAT instances we must update SGs and ensure IP forwarding on the AMI; add that to the runbook as an alternate option.

deploy-bot: terraform apply complete for infra/ams/gpu-networking (plan id: plan-20260310-ams). Outputs:
- transit_gateway_id = tgw-0a1b2c
- vpc_id = vpc-0abc1234
- nat_gateway_ids = [nat-0aa, nat-0bb]
- delegated_zone = ams.redwood-inference.internal

ryan: running route table queries now.

ryan: Route tables look good. All private subnet tables have 0.0.0.0/0 -> tgw-0a1b2c (propagated). Pod CIDR 10.100.0.0/16 present as local.

ryan: NAT GW EIPs attached, tested SNAT from a worker node: `curl -sS https://ifconfig.co` returns expected EIP nat-0aa.

marta: DNS check?

ryan: Parent zone shows NS records delegated to the ams zone and glue records present. `dig @ns-1.parent.int ams.redwood-inference.internal NS +short` returns our name servers.

jules: thanks. Cost mitigation idea: for non-prod clusters convert NATs to a single shared egress VPC with proxy-ing (squid/egress-proxy) — much cheaper if we can tolerate a single egress endpoint in non-prod. We should document tradeoffs in the runbook.

marta: agreed. Add to runbook: production = per-AZ NAT GW HA; non-prod = shared egress with proxy or autoscaling NAT instances. Also note quota limits: EIP quota in account is 5 per region by default, so request increase if we expect many clusters.

ryan: smoke tests:
- curl from bastion to model health => 200 OK
- curl to external IP from worker => shows nat eip
- traceroute to external shows next hop via nat gateway
All green.

marta: OK marking network bring-up as validated pending one handoff action: someone from oncall to take ownership of the ams zone for 48h (monitor BGP flaps we saw). @sung can you take first 24h and escalate to infra-oncall if it reappears?

sung: I can take it. Will add a heartbeat check in s3/monitoring and set an alarm if BGP session flaps more than twice in 15m.

marta: perfect. I'll update the runbook PR with the alternate NAT patterns, quota notes, and a checklist for the oncall. Can we get a quick thumbs up from everyone? :thumbsup:

ryan: :thumbsup:

sung: :thumbsup:

jules: :thumbsup:

marta: thanks all — handing off to oncall.
